## Facts (3):
- [convention] Rerunning CI builds (current) (id: 01a10806-cc79-7463-bbad-83f0a09a17fd; source: shared/human)
  Since 2026-08-12 CI runs on Buildkite; Jenkins was shut down, and PR comments such as `retest this please` do nothing now. To rerun a failed or flaky build, press Retry on the failed job in Buildkite, or run `bk build retry <build-number>` with the number from the PR check.
- [convention] Running the notifier's tests (id: 01a10807-66c8-7ca0-990e-972013ef9e6d; source: shared/human)
  The root test targets never collect services/notifier/tests. Run them from services/notifier with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`: both the root and the notifier have a package named `tests`, and the default import mode resolves the wrong one.
- [convention] Run tests with make test-fast (id: 01a10805-a0a5-7181-ab03-68d80ee2062e; source: shared/human)
  Run `make test-fast` for the unit suite (skips the Postgres and network integration tests). `make test` runs everything but needs `docker compose up db` first.

## Decisions (1):
- [decision] Failed-payment retry schedule (id: 01a10806-3218-7a92-9952-b762665c8bf8; source: shared/human)
  When a charge fails, retry it on days 1, 3, 7, 14 after the failure (contractual, finance policy FP-12). If the day-14 retry also fails, mark the invoice `uncollectible` and stop. Never retry an invoice that has a refund in progress.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

content.text:
CI moved from Jenkins to Buildkite on 2026-08-12, so you rerun the build in Buildkite. You can do it either of two ways:

- **In the Buildkite web page:** open the failed check on your PR, find the failed job and press **Retry**. Only that job runs again, not the whole pipeline.
- **From the command line:** take the build number from the PR check and run:
  ```
  bk build retry <build-number>
  ```

Commenting `retest this please` on the PR no longer does anything, because that only worked with Jenkins.

The team's project memory had two conflicting notes about this: an old one with the Jenkins instructions and a newer one with the Buildkite instructions. I marked the old note as replaced by the newer one so it won't send anyone to Jenkins again. The repo has no CI config or docs about reruns that I could check this against, so these steps come from the team's notes.

If the same test keeps failing on retry, it may be a real failure rather than a flaky one. Run it locally with `make test-fast` to check.
